title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has been empirically shown to enhance the performance of large language models (LLMs) in knowledge-intensive domains such as healthcare, finance, and legal contexts.

defines.name: orthogonal augmentation
defines.definition: A property of dense retrievers in which appending an orthogonal document to a query shifts the resulting embedding in a perpendicular direction while preserving high similarity.

problem: RAG retrieval systems are vulnerable to universal poisoning attacks, and existing embedding-based defenses such as ℓ2 norm or ℓ2 distance fail to reliably detect poisoned documents.
